title: AgentTutor: Empowering Personalized Learning with Multi-Turn Interactive Teaching in Intelligent Education Systems
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a core limitation of many large-language-model-powered intelligent education systems: they typically operate as single-turn question-answering tools and therefore do not continuously assess learner understanding, adapt instruction over time, or support richer personalized teaching. The authors argue that effective tutoring requires multi-turn interaction, ongoing learner assessment, and dynamic adjustment of teaching strategies based on learner progress, cognitive level, goals, preferences, and available study materials.

To address this, the paper introduces AgentTutor, an LLM-based intelligent tutoring architecture built around five modules: curriculum decomposition, learner assessment, dynamic strategy generation, teaching reflection, and knowledge and experience memory. The system uses Bloom's Taxonomy to break curriculum content into hierarchical sub-goals, estimates learner proficiency over time, retrieves and integrates internal and external learning resources, and uses a tree-search-based strategy module to optimize teaching actions. It also supports both interactive dialogue and passive lesson delivery, and stores learner and teaching histories in long-term memory for future personalization.

The empirical evaluation is conducted on benchmark programming datasets (HumanEval and MBPP) using a simulated learner agent rather than real students. The study context is therefore an AI benchmarking and system evaluation environment rather than a real classroom. The learner is initialized at a basic cognitive level and interacts with AgentTutor for 10 turns per benchmark theme. The paper also includes automated evaluations of teaching quality, human expert judgments of pedagogical quality, and ablation studies to test the contribution of each system module.

The main conclusion is that AgentTutor outperforms several prompting and reasoning baselines on benchmark-based learner performance and on measures of interactive teaching quality. The authors conclude that multi-turn, dynamically adaptive tutoring architectures may be more effective than static single-turn systems for personalized learning. However, they also acknowledge important constraints, especially the reliance on simulated learners, limited real-world validation, narrow personalization factors, and still-developing multimodal pedagogy generation.

identified_tools.name: AgentTutor
identified_tools.description: An LLM-powered multi-turn interactive intelligent education system for personalized learning, built as a multi-agent tutoring framework with curriculum decomposition, learner assessment, dynamic strategy generation, teaching reflection, and long-term memory.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a personalized tutoring system for programming instruction on HumanEval and MBPP, where it interacted for 10 turns with a simulated learner and adapted teaching strategies based on learner cognitive level and progress.

findings.finding_summary: On the HumanEval benchmark, AgentTutor achieved Pass@1 of 92.7 with GPT-3.5-turbo and 96.9 with GPT-4, outperforming reported baselines including CoT (46.9), ReAct (56.9), ToT (54.4), RAP (63.1), Reflexion (68.1) for GPT-3.5-turbo, and zero-shot GPT-4 (80.1) and Reflexion GPT-4 (91.0). The paper interprets this as improved learner performance after multi-turn tutoring interactions.
findings.measure: Pass@1 accuracy on HumanEval programming benchmark

findings.finding_summary: On the MBPP benchmark, AgentTutor achieved Pass@1 of 89.4 with GPT-3.5-turbo, exceeding CoT (54.9), ReAct (67.0), ToT (65.8), RAP (71.4), and Reflexion (70.0). The study presents this as evidence that dynamic teaching strategies and multi-turn interactions improve programming-task performance.
findings.measure: Pass@1 accuracy on MBPP programming benchmark

findings.finding_summary: For interactive teaching quality, AgentTutor outperformed CoT, ToT, and Reflexion on conversational adaptability, feedback quality, and question difficulty using Prometheus 2 scored on a 5-point rubric. Exact numeric scores are not reported in the text excerpt, but the figure and narrative state AgentTutor was highest across all three metrics.
findings.measure: Prometheus 2 5-point rubric scores for conversational adaptability, feedback quality, and question difficulty

findings.finding_summary: In human evaluation by three teaching experts, AgentTutor received the most favorable ratings versus CoT, ToT, and Reflexion on accuracy, conversational quality, helpfulness/relevance, and question set quality using a 3-point scale. The paper attributes these results to AgentTutor’s multi-turn interaction design and alignment with learner level.
findings.measure: Human expert ratings on accuracy, conversational quality, helpfulness/relevance, and question set quality

findings.finding_summary: Ablation on HumanEval with GPT-3.5-turbo showed all modules contributed to performance: full AgentTutor scored 92.7 Pass@1; removing DSM reduced performance to 72.9 (-19.8), removing CDM to 84.1 (-8.6), removing KEMM to 85.3 (-7.4), removing LAM to 85.7 (-7.0), and removing TRM to 86.2 (-6.5). The largest drop came from removing the Dynamic Strategy Module.
findings.measure: Pass@1 accuracy under module ablations on HumanEval

identified_tools.description: Alibaba Qwen-family multimodal large language model.
identified_tools.use_case: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct was used as the multimodal component for processing study materials in the AgentTutor system.

identified_tools.name: LLaMA
identified_tools.description: Meta LLaMA-family large language models, including instruction-tuned variants used for fine-tuning conversational behavior.
identified_tools.use_case: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct was used to train AgentTutor’s conversational teaching model with LoRA and DPO on tutoring datasets.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical system paper with benchmark experiments, automated evaluation, human ratings, and ablations, but it relies on simulated learners rather than real students and does not report randomized or quasi-experimental causal evidence in authentic educational settings.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports strong benchmark gains and favorable teaching-quality evaluations, but effects are not reported as standard educational effect sizes and the real-world learning impact on actual students remains unclear.
